exposure: gestational age (preterm birth vs. term birth)
outcome: anti-pertussis toxin (PT) IgG antibody levels in cord blood
anti-filamentous hemagglutinin (FHA) IgG antibody levels in cord blood
placental transfer rates of anti-PT IgG
placental transfer rates of anti-FHA IgG
cohort: The study included 194 pregnant women who delivered preterm (before 37 weeks) and 140 pregnant women who delivered at term, along with their respective umbilical cord blood and maternal blood samples.
finding: Placental antibody transfer rates increased with gestational age, but both transfer rates and antibody levels were generally low, especially in infants born before 32 weeks gestation.
birth_weight: Measured as a factor positively correlated with antibody transfer rates.
gest_age: Included preterm (before 37 weeks) and term infants, with specific analysis for those before 32 weeks gestation; gestational age was also a measured correlating factor.
